channel.title: Ryan Pennell · Tangents & Demos
channel.description: New articles and interactive demos from Ryan Pennell, Ivy Tech Bloomington.

item.title: Which Way Does the Ellipse Stretch?
item.description: The bigger denominator wins. Drag the denominators under x² and y² and watch the ellipse stretch horizontally, vertically, or become a circle, with the half-axes, a, b, c, and the foci marked.

item.title: The Ambiguous Case (SSA): Why 0, 1, or 2 Triangles?
item.description: Given angle A, side a, and side b, swing side a around vertex C and count where it lands. The Law of Sines work updates as you drag, showing when sin B is too big, when there's exactly one right triangle, and when both B and 180° − B fit.

item.title: Cleo’s Integrals
item.description: An anonymous Math Stack Exchange user posted 39 correct closed forms with no work shown. The math behind the golden-ratio and Airy integrals, and how experimental mathematics finds answers before proofs.

item.title: The Squeeze Theorem, ε–δ Style
item.description: The proof as a picture: find δ for the lower bound, δ for the upper bound, take the smaller one, and the trapped function has nowhere to go. Examples include x² sin(1/x) and sin x/x, plus one where the bounds disagree and the theorem says nothing.

item.title: The ε–δ Definition of a Limit
item.description: Play the limit game: your opponent picks ε, you answer with δ. Drag on the graph to watch where the function stays in the band and where it escapes, for limits that work (x², sin x/x, x sin(1/x)) and ones that fail (a jump, sin(1/x)), or type in your own function.

item.title: Is π^π^π^π an Integer?
item.description: Nobody knows. Checking numerically would take about 6.66 × 10^17 digits of π, over 2,000 times the current record, and the classical transcendence theorems don't apply. What can be proved: no two consecutive terms of the tower are rational, and Schanuel's conjecture would settle it.

item.title: Radix Economy and the Number e
item.description: If a digit with b states costs b, which base is cheapest? The continuous answer is e, the best integer base is 3 (it comes down to 8 < 9), no mix of integer radices beats pure ternary, and base e itself can't write 10 in finitely many digits.

item.title: Subtraction Without Borrowing: The Method of Complements in Any Base
item.description: Turn subtraction into addition in any base: complement the digits, add one, add, and drop the leading carry. A short proof, what a missing carry means, the modular view, and a mixed-radix version that covers clock times, feet and inches, pounds and ounces, and mixed numbers.
